# Using an external DEM

Terrain correction needs a digital elevation model (DEM). By default SNAP
downloads the Copernicus 30 m DEM by itself, so most users never need this
page. Use an external DEM when a better local one exists, such as a national
elevation model, or to avoid SNAP's
[height error](snap-processing.qmd#corrections-s1bursts-applies) with the
built-in Copernicus DEM.

## Prepare the DEM

An external DEM must be prepared before SNAP reads it, because SNAP has two
reported problems with external DEMs:

- **It samples them half a pixel off**, to the south-east
  ([forum report](https://forum.step.esa.int/t/external-dem-is-sampled-half-a-pixel-off/46042)).
  SNAP fixed this in the 14.0.2 update of its DEM module.
- **It knows only one height reference, EGM96**, which most modern DEMs do not
  use ([forum report](https://forum.step.esa.int/t/copernicus-dem-built-in-path-applies-egm96-while-the-data-is-egm2008/46041)).

`prepare_dem_for_snap()` corrects both and writes a copy, leaving your original
untouched:

```{.python}
from pathlib import Path
from s1bursts import prepare_dem_for_snap

prepared = prepare_dem_for_snap(
    Path("swissalti3d_30m.tif"),
    source_crs="EPSG:2056+5728",
    download_missing_grids=True,
)
```

`source_crs` states both the map projection and the height reference of the
DEM, joined by `+`. Here, `EPSG:2056` is the Swiss LV95 grid and `5728` the
Swiss LN02 heights; look these up in your DEM's documentation. Converting the
heights can need correction grids from PROJ, which
`download_missing_grids=True` fetches when they are freely available.

The half-pixel shift is applied only for SNAP versions that still need it.
`prepare_dem_for_snap()` checks the SNAP installation it finds the same way
processing does, so the prepared copy is correct only for that installation and
only for SNAP. Prepared copies are cached, so preparing the same file again
costs nothing.

## Use the prepared DEM

Pass the prepared file to the processing settings, together with a short name.
The name is written into every product's metadata, so you can tell later which
DEM was used. It also lets a rerun check that an existing product was made with
the same DEM before skipping it; without a name, that check is left out:

```{.python}
from s1bursts import RTCConfig

config = RTCConfig(
    dem=prepared,
    dem_name="swissALTI3D 30 m",
    external_dem_apply_egm=False,
)
```

Keep `external_dem_apply_egm=False`: the preparation has already converted the
heights, and SNAP would otherwise convert them a second time.

## Downsample a fine DEM first

SNAP's terrain flattening and terrain correction (geocoding) take much longer
on a fine DEM grid. So a DEM much finer than your products should be downsampled before
preparing it, by averaging all fine pixels within each coarse one.
freezebase's `vrt.warp()`
averages by default; this reduces the 2 m swissALTI3D to 30 m:

```{.python}
from freezebase import vrt
from freezebase.raster import write_cog

write_cog(vrt.warp("swissalti3d_2m.tif", resolution=30), "swissalti3d_30m.tif")
```
